learning_outcomes.text: Understand, evaluate and analyze the different forms of representation and simplification of logical functions, as well as the mastery of the most usual numbering systems used in digital.
Analyze, simulate and synthesize combinational circuits, and select the most appropriate technology according to the initial specifications.
Simulate and design asynchronous and synchronous sequential circuits, based on given specifications, as well as detect faults in circuits and propose appropriate solutions in each case.

Implement complete low-medium complexity systems, including sequential/combinational circuits and appropriate I/O stages; select the most suitable commercial components, from a technical and economic point of view, all based on a problem specified by a client.
Work in a group, reason critically to compare various solutions and discriminate the most optimal one.
Implement circuit designs in a structured way, dividing into simpler sub-circuits and their subsequent integration into a superior one, based on given specifications.

syllabus_topics: Representation of signed and unsigned binary numbers
Interface between TTL and CMOS families
Synthesis of combinational circuits with logic gates
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 4.0 out of 10 is required in the theoretical block. The final grade is calculated as 0.6*Theory_Exam + 0.1*(Practical_Exam_P1 + Practical_Exam_P2) + 0.04*(T1+T2+T3+T4+T5). If the minimum in theory is not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary June/July call, theoretical exam minimum 4.0; practical and assignment grades are kept. For the extraordinary December/January call, a minimum grade of 4.0 on the theoretical exam is required. The final grade is calculated as 0.6*Theory_Exam + 0.4*Practical_Exam (new practical exam).
